content_record.title: Mitochondria hand protons to lysosomes: a new acidification pathway that fails with age
content_record.editorial_body: A conserved mechanism shows mitochondrial proton export via membrane contacts drives lysosomal acidification; aging disrupts this coupling, but engineered links restore it. Mitochondria-lysosome contacts transfer protons to acidify lysosomes. Aging disrupts contacts, causing lysosomal de-acidification and senescence. Restoring contacts reverses senescence and restores autophagic flux. This signal is based on Mitochondria-lysosome coupling contributes to lysosome acidification and aging. from PubMed. Read the original report for full context.
